reports.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Analysis Reveals Exercise-Induced Transcriptional Dynamics in Half-Marathon Runners
reports.authors: Veschetti L; Patuzzo C; Treccani M; Moron Dalla Tor L; Deiana M; Cheri S; Griggio F; Lippi G; Schena F; De Santis D; Dalle Carbonare L; Tarperi C; Trabetti E; Valenti MT; Malerba G
reports.version_date: Accepted 7 January 2025 (masthead: Received 9 Aug 2024; Revised 31 Dec 2024; Accepted 7 Jan 2025); published Scand J Med Sci Sports 2025;35:e70018. No separate online-first date stated.
reports.inclusion_reason: Single identifiable acute exercise bout (21.1 km half marathon, 'Run 4 Science' event, April 2019) with a pre-exercise baseline sample (90-60 min before start) and an immediate post-exercise sample (15-30 min after arrival); PBMC/platelet scRNAseq satisfies the immune-cell-omics linkage rule; adults (29+/-5 y). Meets Core A per contract 2.1-2.2 (p.2 Methods 2.1).
reports.reviewer_notes: AI stand-in for reviewer C, 10-report charting pilot only (per pilot convention, C uses the '_B' screening slot; reviewer_A left null). Candidate study-family overlap with an earlier 2016 Run 4 Science cohort (ref.35) is unresolved; see study_families.study_notes and unresolved_questions.
reports.author_stated_use: 'may inform future training routines or nutritional guidelines based on individual gene expression levels' (Abstract, p.1); Conclusion p.9 adds 'highlights the importance of considering individual responses to exercise in the development of personalized training regimens.' Framed as a proposed future application, not a use the study itself tested.
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.9 Conclusion: 'myeloid cells display a stress response and harbor active viral processes, supporting the "open window" hypothesis'; term also defined in p.2 Introduction.

cohorts.cohort_label: Half-marathon amateur runners, Verona 'Run 4 Science' 2019 event (2 of 4 analyzed after QC)
cohorts.baseline_health: 'self-reportedly healthy males and females' (p.2 Methods 2.1); no explicit active-infection screen described beyond self-report; no clinical/metabolic-disease exclusion criterion stated.
cohorts.age_sex: Four age-matched amateur runners, two males and two females, 29+/-5 years (mean+/-SD) (p.2 Methods 2.1).
cohorts.training_status: NR (described only as 'amateur runners'; no categorical training-status classification reported)
cohorts.cohort_notes: Randomly selected from ~100 individuals present at the 2019 'Run 4 Science' half-marathon event in Verona, Italy; only constraint was self-reported health within the same age range (p.2 Methods 2.1). Of the 4 recruited, 1 participant's samples were excluded before sequencing for insufficient library quality (p.2 Methods 2.1), and a further participant's samples were excluded after sequencing QC for insufficient high-quality cells (p.2-3 Methods 2.3), leaving 2 donors (paired pre/post) in the final analysis. Confirmed against Supplement Table_S2, which lists exactly 4 samples: pre_1, pre_2, post_1, post_2 (2 donors x 2 timepoints), and whose summed cell counts (299+1110+954+1848=4211) match the text's '4211 cells... deemed high-quality' (p.3).
cohorts.age_range: 29 +/- 5 years (mean +/- SD); no explicit min-max range reported (p.2 Methods 2.1).

report_cohort_links.report_specific_population: 4 enrolled amateur runners; 2 contributed paired pre/post samples to the final scRNAseq analysis after two sequential QC exclusions (1 at library-prep stage, 1 at cell-QC stage). Cluster differential-abundance analyses (edgeR; Tables S2-S3) likewise use only these 2 donors x 2 timepoints = 4 samples.
report_cohort_links.link_notes: The main text never states the final analysed n directly; n_analyzed=2 is derived by cross-referencing two QC-exclusion sentences (Methods 2.1 and 2.3) with Supplement Table_S2's sample list (pre_1, pre_2, post_1, post_2) and the matching total cell count (4211). It is not fully certain from the text alone that the two exclusion sentences describe two distinct runners rather than the same runner twice, though the supplement's 4-sample list and the paper's enrolled n=4 make 2 excluded / 2 analysed the most consistent reading. Flagged in unresolved_questions.

sample_sets.group_condition: Exercise arm (own pre-exercise baseline serves as within-subject comparator; no non-exercise control group)
sample_sets.dose: 21.1 km half marathon ('Run 4 Science', Verona, April 2019)
sample_sets.control: Pre-exercise baseline (paired, within-subject); no separate non-exercise control group
sample_sets.exercise_end_definition: NA for this baseline row; for the study overall, exercise end = arrival at the finish line (race completion).
sample_sets.timepoint_as_reported: 'Pre run blood sampling occurred 90-60 min before the scheduled start time of 9 a.m.' (p.2 Methods 2.1)
sample_sets.matrix: PBMC (Ficoll-Paque density-gradient isolation from venous blood); residual/co-isolated platelets identified as a separate cluster within the same scRNAseq dataset
sample_sets.assay_platform: Droplet-based single-cell RNA-seq (Bio-Rad ddSEQ Single-Cell Isolator, Illumina Bio-Rad SureCell WTA 3' Library Prep Kit; sequenced on Illumina NextSeq 500)
sample_sets.repeated_sampling: Same 2 donors sampled again post-exercise (paired design); no repeated baseline beyond this single pre-exercise timepoint.
sample_sets.pairing_structure: Paired by donor ID across pre/post timepoints (same 2 individuals); DESeq2 paired design, pre-run used as base level (p.2 Methods 2.5).
sample_sets.age_sex_stratum: NA (results not stratified by sex; small n precluded stratification)
sample_sets.preanalytics: Blood collected by venipuncture; PBMCs purified by Ficoll-Paque density-gradient centrifugation within max 2 h after sampling; samples kept at 10-15C; PBMCs resuspended in 1x PBS-0.1% filtered BSA and held at 5-10C up to 1 h before library preparation; libraries sequenced the following day (p.2 Methods 2.1-2.2).
sample_sets.normalization: SCTransform workflow in Seurat (IntegrateData); batch effect, mitochondrial expression and cell-cycle effect explored as confounders and corrected during integration (p.2-3 Methods 2.3).
sample_sets.circadian: Pre-run sampling 90-60 min before the 9 a.m. start (approx. 7:30-8:30 a.m.); differs in time-of-day from the post sample (approx. 11:45 a.m.-12:30 p.m.), but this difference is inherent to bracketing the single exercise bout, not separately controlled (p.2 Methods 2.1).
sample_sets.missing_data: 1 of 4 recruited runners excluded before sequencing (insufficient library quality); a further runner excluded after sequencing QC (insufficient high-quality cells); 2 donors remain (p.2 Methods 2.1; p.2-3 Methods 2.3).
sample_sets.cell_context: 9 annotated PBMC/platelet cell types via SCType Immune System marker database (classical monocytes, non-classical monocytes, myeloid dendritic cells, NK cells, CD8+ NKT-like cells, memory CD4+ T cells, naive CD4+ T cells, naive B cells, platelets) plus an 'Unknown' cluster (p.3 Methods 2.4; Figure 1).
sample_sets.sample_notes: Exact clock time of the pre-run draw is not given beyond the '90-60 min before start' window; sex of the 2 finally-analysed donors is not separately reported.
sample_sets.exercise_duration: NR (individual finishing times for the 21.1 km half marathon not reported)

sample_sets.dose: 21.1 km half marathon ('Run 4 Science', Verona, April 2019)
sample_sets.exercise_end_definition: Arrival at the finish line (race completion)
sample_sets.timepoint_as_reported: 'post run blood sampling was performed 15-30 min after arrival, approximately 3h after the start time (11:45-12:30 a.m.)' (p.2 Methods 2.1)
sample_sets.matrix: PBMC (Ficoll-Paque density-gradient isolation from venous blood); residual/co-isolated platelets identified as a separate cluster within the same scRNAseq dataset
sample_sets.assay_platform: Droplet-based single-cell RNA-seq (Bio-Rad ddSEQ Single-Cell Isolator, SureCell WTA 3' Library Prep Kit; Illumina NextSeq 500)
sample_sets.repeated_sampling: Same 2 donors as the pre-exercise sample (paired design)
sample_sets.pairing_structure: Paired by donor ID with the pre-exercise sample (same 2 individuals); DESeq2 paired design, pre-run = base level.
sample_sets.preanalytics: Identical handling to the pre-run sample: venipuncture, Ficoll-Paque PBMC isolation within 2h, storage at 10-15C, PBS-BSA resuspension, up to 1h hold before library prep (p.2 Methods 2.1-2.2).
sample_sets.normalization: SCTransform workflow in Seurat (IntegrateData); batch/mitochondrial/cell-cycle confounders corrected (p.2-3 Methods 2.3).
sample_sets.circadian: Sampled approx. 11:45 a.m.-12:30 p.m., approx. 3h after the scheduled 9 a.m. start (p.2 Methods 2.1); the '15-30 min after arrival' window straddles the 0_to_lt30min / 30min_to_lt3h bin boundary, see sample_notes.
sample_sets.missing_data: Same QC exclusion chain as the pre-exercise sample (see SS-R61-01); 2 donors contribute to this timepoint.
sample_sets.cell_context: Same 9 annotated cell types plus 'Unknown' cluster (Figure 1); differential-abundance analysis (Figure 3, Tables S2-S3) found no statistically significant compositional shift between pre and post, though a non-significant trend toward myeloid dendritic cell enrichment was noted (p=0.09) (p.4 Results 3.4).
sample_sets.sample_notes: Reported window '15-30 min after arrival' straddles the within_organising_window 0_to_lt30min / 30min_to_lt3h bin boundary; binned here as 0_to_lt30min because the stated range is predominantly <30 min and the paper's own framing throughout is 'immediate post'; flagged as an UNCLEAR edge case (see unresolved_questions).

analyte_id.original_label: whole transcriptome, per-cluster pseudobulk (single-cell analysis approach)

measurements.platform: Droplet scRNA-seq (ddSeeker/STARsolo/Seurat), aggregated per annotated cluster into pseudobulk counts; DESeq2 paired DEA per cell type (p.2 Methods 2.5)
measurements.cell_context: 9 annotated clusters analysed separately (classical monocytes, non-classical monocytes, myeloid dendritic cells, NK cells, CD8+ NKT-like cells, memory CD4+ T cells, naive CD4+ T cells, naive B cells, platelets)
measurements.assay_validity: QC: cells removed if UMI counts <200, gene counts <200, or >20% mitochondrial UMIs; genes not detected in >=10 cells across the dataset discarded; batch/mitochondrial/cell-cycle effects corrected via Seurat SCTransform + IntegrateData (p.2 Methods 2.3)
measurements.feature_identification: NR (final retained gene count after the >=10-cell filter is not numerically stated in the text)
measurements.comparison: Post-run vs pre-run, paired design, pre-run as DESeq2 reference level, evaluated separately within each of the 9 annotated cell-type clusters
measurements.effect_uncertainty: Significance threshold: Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p<0.05 and |log2FC|>0.58
measurements.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction applied within each cell-type cluster
measurements.confounding: Batch effect, mitochondrial expression and cell-cycle effect modelled as confounders and corrected (p.2-3 Methods 2.3)
measurements.donor_level_inference: Pseudobulk-per-cluster aggregation used specifically so that DESeq2's negative-binomial model treats donors (n=2), not single cells, as the statistical replicate per cluster (p.2 Methods 2.5).
measurements.missing_data: See sample_sets.missing_data (2 of 4 enrolled donors excluded before this analysis: 1 at library-prep QC, 1 at cell-level QC)
measurements.null_findings: No significantly modulated genes detected in myeloid dendritic cells or non-classical monocytes after multiple-testing correction (p.3 Results 3.1)
measurements.reported_feature_count: 23 DEGs in classical monocytes; 3 DEGs across lymphoid-lineage cell types; 0 in myeloid dendritic cells and non-classical monocytes (Table 1, p.3 Results 3.1-3.2)
measurements.measurement_notes: Assay-level summary for the paper's primary 'single-cell analysis approach' (cluster-resolved pseudobulk DESeq2, Methods 2.5). The complete tested gene universe (all genes passing the >=10-cell filter, not only the significant ones in Table 1) is not numerically stated anywhere in the main text or accessible supplement; tested_universe_n is therefore NR rather than inferred. Named-candidate rows below cover a representative, not exhaustive, subset of the genes tabulated as significant in Table 1 (23+3 named genes across cell types) and Table 2 (27 genes); exhaustively transcribing every gene x cell-type cell of Table 1/Table 2/Supplement Table S1 (1348 GSEA pathway rows)/Table S4 was judged out of proportion for this pilot timebox (see unresolved_questions).
measurements.tested_universe: All expressed genes detected in >=10 single cells across the whole dataset, ranked by log2FoldChange and tested per annotated cluster via DESeq2 (negative-binomial model, paired design, pre-run as base level)
feature_universe_locator: p.2-3 Methods 2.3 (gene filter: detected in >=10 cells)
measurements.candidate_in_original_aims_methods: NA (assay-universe row; see individual named-candidate rows)

analyte_id.original_label: whole transcriptome, whole-sample pseudobulk (all cells as one cluster)

measurements.platform: Droplet scRNA-seq data re-analysed as simulated bulk RNA-seq (all cells pooled into a single pseudobulk sample per donor/timepoint); DESeq2 paired DEA (p.3 Methods 2.7)
measurements.cell_context: All cells treated as belonging to a single pseudobulk cluster (no cell-type resolution)
measurements.assay_validity: Same QC pipeline and thresholds as the cluster-resolved approach; Methods 2.7 states 'the methodology and parameters used in the analyses are the same as the ones described for scRNAseq data'
measurements.comparison: Post-run vs pre-run, paired design, pre-run as DESeq2 reference level, whole-sample pseudobulk (no cell-type split)
measurements.effect_uncertainty: Significance threshold: adjusted p<0.05 and |log2FC|>0.58
measurements.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction
measurements.confounding: Same confounders as the cluster-level approach (batch, mitochondrial, cell-cycle)
measurements.donor_level_inference: Whole-sample pseudobulk aggregation; statistical unit = donor (n=2); authors note this approach can gain statistical power for some genes but loses cell-type-specific resolution for others (p.7-8 Discussion)
measurements.null_findings: Results broadly concordant with the cluster-resolved single-cell approach for 12 of 27 genes (Table S4), but the pseudobulk approach 'indicates a loss of power to detect modulated pathways when compared to a single-cell approach' (p.8 Discussion)
measurements.reported_feature_count: 27 DEGs (Table 2); 12 of these also significant in the single-cell cluster-resolved approach, 15 significant only via pseudobulk (p.4 Results 3.5; Table S4)
measurements.measurement_notes: Second, distinct assay-level approach ('Pseudo-Bulk Analysis', Methods 2.7) simulating a conventional bulk RNA-seq experiment from the same underlying scRNAseq data; kept as a separate assay_universe_id from the cluster-resolved approach because the unit of analysis (whole sample vs per-cluster) differs even though the raw data and donors are identical.
measurements.tested_universe: All expressed genes passing the same >=10-cell detection filter, tested on whole-sample (single-cluster) pseudobulk counts via DESeq2

precision_validation.replication: No technical replicates, repeat library preparations, spike-ins or assay reliability statistics (ICC/CV) are reported for the scRNAseq assay itself.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: QC thresholds (UMI/gene/mitochondrial-content cutoffs, batch/cell-cycle correction) are described, but no formal analytical-reliability metric (technical-replicate concordance, ICC, CV) is reported for the assay. Marker family in play: immune_cell_transcriptome.

precision_validation.response_evidence: Pre-run baseline and a single immediate post-run sample (15-30 min after arrival); both within the organising window (pre_exercise_baseline and 0_to_lt30min bins).
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Only one post-exercise time bin is sampled (0_to_lt30min); no further recovery timepoints (e.g. 24-72h) are available to chart the return-to-baseline trajectory that the authors themselves note (citing Yu et al. [14], >24h needed to reach baseline, p.9 Discussion).

9 immune/megakaryocyte cell types annotated via the SCType 'Immune system' marker database give cell-type-resolved transcriptomic specificity; however a substantial 'Unknown' cluster (Figure 3) and the inclusion of non-leukocyte platelets reduce overall specificity of the panel as a whole.

precision_validation.individualization: No repeated-baseline or repeated-bout sampling; only n=2 donors in the final analysis; authors explicitly state the small sample size 'might restrict the generalizability and reliability of the results' and call for more individuals in future work (p.9 Discussion).
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Inter-individual variation is plausible given the biology described but is not quantified (no ICC/CV/responder-consistency statistic); with n=2, individual-level claims cannot be distinguished from noise. Authors describe only a qualitative 'complex dynamics attributable to different actors', not an individualized-marker claim.

precision_validation.functional_evidence: No direct in vitro/ex vivo/in vivo immune-function assay (e.g. cytotoxicity, phagocytosis) was performed; GO pathway enrichment (viral process, stress response, coagulation pathways) is annotation-level only, which the extraction manual explicitly excludes from counting as measured immune function.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: No clinical/infection follow-up and no functional assay; only transcriptomic and GO pathway-annotation evidence, narratively interpreted as consistent with the 'open window' or 'acute stress-induced immunoenhancement' hypotheses but not functionally or clinically tested.

precision_validation.replication: Single cohort, single report; no technical or biological replication beyond the paired n=2 donors. Authors narratively note concordance of specific genes/pathways with prior literature (Yu et al. [14], Condeminas et al. [15], Maqueda et al. [29]), but this is cross-study narrative corroboration of overlapping gene names, not a formal independent re-test of this report's candidates.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: No independent cohort or external dataset formally re-tests this report's specific DEGs/pathways with the same definitions; validation_split=none.

precision_validation.field_feasibility: 'Even though we analyzed a small number of samples due to the high cost of single-cell sequencing...' (p.9 Perspective) - an explicit cost/throughput barrier reported for scRNAseq as a method, directly limiting sample size.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Authors explicitly discuss cost as a practical constraint on sample size/throughput; this is a direct feasibility statement about the assay itself (lab-only, not point-of-care), not a formal field-use or turnaround-time test.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Single identifiable acute bout (21.1 km half-marathon, April 2019) with a pre-run baseline and an immediate post-run sample (15-30 min after arrival; p.2-3 Methods 2.1), within the 0-72h organising window and with no exposure threshold required (contract 2.1-2.2). Direct immune-cell transcriptome (scRNAseq of PBMCs annotated into 9 immune/megakaryocyte cell types; p.3 Methods 2.4) satisfies the immune-linkage rule as immune_cell_omics.

unresolved_questions: Final analysed donor count (n=2 of 4 enrolled) can only be confirmed by cross-referencing two separate QC-exclusion sentences (Methods 2.1: library quality; Methods 2.3: cell quality) against the supplement's sample list (Table_S2: pre_1/pre_2/post_1/post_2) and matching cell-count arithmetic (299+1110+954+1848=4211). The main text never states the final n directly, and it is not fully certain the two sentences describe two distinct runners rather than the same runner described twice at two pipeline stages. The manual should specify whether reviewers may back-calculate n_analyzed from a supplement/figure-caption arithmetic check when the main text omits it, and how confident such a derivation must be before it counts as 'reported' rather than 'UNCLEAR'.

The post-run sampling window ('15-30 min after arrival', p.2 Methods 2.1) straddles the 0_to_lt30min / 30min_to_lt3h time_bin boundary. The manual/time_bin_rules do not specify how to bin a reported range that itself spans a bin edge; this sample was binned as 0_to_lt30min on narrative grounds ('immediate post' framing throughout the paper) rather than a rule.

The marker_family controlled vocabulary has no category for non-leukocyte blood-cell transcriptome (platelets/megakaryocyte lineage, e.g. PF4, PPBP, CAVIN2) or for mitochondrial/heat-shock/general stress-response genes (MT-CO1, MT-CO2, HSP90AA1, HSPA8) that recur in this discovery-omics dataset; 'other' was used as a default, which may undercount the immune_cell_transcriptome family in downstream figures.

This report's omics design (unbiased single-cell/pseudobulk discovery, not a pre-specified immune-candidate panel) makes the dictionary's default candidate_selection_rule value (all_named_immune_candidates_from_original_aims_methods_regardless_of_significance) a poor fit, because the authors only name genes that already passed their significance filter; 'author_reported_feature_set' was used instead, which is defensible but was a judgement call the manual does not make explicit for discovery-omics designs.

Row-volume/feasibility: this report tabulates 23+3 significant genes x up to 5 cell types (Table 1), 27 genes (Table 2), a 41-row cross-method overlap table (Supplement Table_S4), and 1348 GSEA pathway rows (Supplement Table_S1). This pilot extracted 2 assay-universe rows + 59 representative named-candidate/result rows (all of Table 1 and Table 2 verbatim, plus 1 GSEA example) but did not transcribe the full 1348-row GSEA table or attempt to recover the untested/non-significant background transcriptome (not individually named by the authors). The manual should state an explicit row-volume policy for very large omics result tables (e.g. 'transcribe all named/tabulated results; summarise pathway-level GSEA tables with a representative subset and a locator to the full supplement table' or require full transcription).
